components.css: .ds-cta-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 17px; text-decoration: none; color: #ff8e00; transition: gap 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-cta-text { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 15.2px; font-weight: 400; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.4px; text-shadow: 0 0 3px #ff8e00; } .ds-cta-arrow { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-cta-link:hover { gap: 24px; } .ds-cta-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ff8e00; outline-offset: 4px; }

narrative.overview: This is a designer's flight deck. A near-black void holds content the way a HUD holds telemetry; signal orange marks the one action worth taking, terminal green is reserved for live readouts. But it is not cold sci-fi: the void is warmed from below by an earth band of terracotta, umber, and ember-brown, so the cosmos feels watched from a lived-in place. Film grain and a spaceship cursor make the surface feel like a physical instrument. Components are tactile and confident, with real weight and long-eased motion. The cosmic frame sets the ambition; the work inside the cards stays the hero.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black space body warmed by an earth band (terracotta/umber/ember)
Signal orange as the single action color; terminal green as the live-data color
Glassmorphic navigation and overlays, used purposefully
Film grain + spaceship cursor as ambient instrument texture
Tactile components with real weight and long-eased motion
Inter for structure, Questrial for display warmth, monospace for telemetry

rules.name: The Single Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal orange is an action color, not a brand wash. It appears on the one thing the user should do next and nowhere else. If two oranges compete on a screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Live-Green Rule
rules.body: Terminal green is forbidden as decoration. It is permitted only where something is genuinely live or measured: a status, a readout, a real-time response. Green used for 'looks techy' is a tell.

rules.name: The One Shout Rule
rules.body: Only the hero headline is allowed to fill the viewport. Below the fold, scale steps down hard; nothing else competes with the opening shout.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are brown-black, never neutral gray. A gray drop-shadow on this palette reads as a 2014 app card and is forbidden.

dos: Do keep signal orange (#ff8e00) as the single action color — one obvious next move per screen.
Do reserve terminal green (#4ade80) for genuinely live or measured states only.
Do warm every shadow toward brown-black (#0d0600), never neutral gray.
Do keep text on Ink Cream (#d6d0c4), warm and never pure white, to tie type to the earth band.
Do give interactive elements real weight and long-eased motion — tactile and confident.
Do let only the hero headline fill the viewport; step scale down hard below it.
donts: Don't ship the generic template portfolio look — no interchangeable Webflow hero, no uniform card grid without a point of view.
Don't drift toward a corporate SaaS landing — no navy-and-blue gradient wash, no hero-metric blocks, no buzzword copy.
Don't use terminal green decoratively to 'look techy' — it must mean live or measured.
Don't let a second orange compete with the primary action on any screen.
Don't use a neutral gray drop-shadow; on this warm palette it reads as a 2014 app card.
Don't let cosmic effects out-shout the work — the project is always the hero.
